neighbours.label: The verb or auxiliary right after the subject in an instructional science question ('did your measured value [agree] with…', 'What [happens] when…', 'Why [does] the encoder…', 'What clues [can] you identify')
fire: Did your measured value agree with the accepted value for pi, and what might explain any difference?
Ask the children what colors they can make by mixing two. What happens when they mix three or more colors?
How are negative numbers represented? Why does the encoder always start near zero when you turn it?
Look at the photo on the right. What clues can you identify that suggest why the camp was moved?
Which way is heat transferred, to the system or from it, when the gas is compressed?
If you double the length of the pendulum, what happens to the period of its swing?
Does the data support your hypothesis, and which results would you need to repeat?
Why does the ice melt faster on the metal plate than on the wooden one in the experiment?
quiet: Your measured value agreed with the accepted value for pi, which might be explained by the careful setup.
The children mixed two colors and then three or more, and the teacher wrote down what they made.
The encoder always starts near zero when you turn it, and negative numbers are shown with a sign bit.
Look at the photo on the right. The clues suggest that the camp was moved after the flood.
Heat is transferred from the system to the surroundings when the gas is compressed in the cylinder.
When the length of the pendulum is doubled, the period of its swing grows by about forty percent.
The data support the hypothesis, and the results should be repeated in a second trial next week.
The ice melts faster on the metal plate than on the wooden one in the experiment, as expected.
